svg.title: Figure 2. Compact normal quotients preserve the absence of connected solvable normal subgroups
svg.desc: A vertical proof schematic for Section 1A of Almost-connected groups and the solvable radical. A connected locally compact Hausdorff group G with no nontrivial connected solvable normal subgroup and an arbitrary compact normal subgroup K are considered. Connected conjugation fixes irreducible character classes. All finite sets F of irreducible representations give invariant kernels N_F and compact Lie models K/N_F. A matrix normalizer calculation checks every disconnected component of each model; continuous implementer cosets give inner actions. Closed implementer sets have the finite intersection property, so one element of K implements conjugation by each fixed g on all of K, giving G=K C_G(K). The centralizer quotient by Z(K) is homeomorphic to G/K. The compact-kernel component theorem uses totally disconnected quotients and van Dantzig. A connected solvable normal subgroup P lifts to a closed normal solvable E in the centralizer, with compact central kernel Z(K). Its identity component is trivial by the assumption on G, while it surjects onto P, so P is trivial. Finite-model and orthogonal-projection sketches are abstractions, not an exhaustion or a geometric model of K.
